questions.q: What problem does a Namespace primarily solve for Northbridge's shared cluster?
options: It makes Pods start faster
It gives every team unlimited CPU and memory
It scopes names, quotas, and RBAC rules so teams sharing one cluster don't collide or spill into each other's objects
It replaces the need for Deployments
questions.explain: Namespaces divide one physical cluster into virtual ones, each with its own naming scope — preventing collisions and giving a boundary for quotas and RBAC.

questions.q: Which command permanently changes kubectl's default namespace so you stop typing -n on every command?
options: kubectl create namespace analytics
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=analytics
kubectl delete namespace analytics
questions.explain: kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=<name> updates the active context's default namespace.

questions.q: Which of these is a cluster-scoped resource, NOT tied to any single Namespace?
options: Pod
ConfigMap
PersistentVolume
Secret
questions.explain: PersistentVolumes (along with Nodes, StorageClasses, and Namespaces themselves) are cluster-scoped. Pods, ConfigMaps, and Secrets are namespaced.

questions.q: What does a ResourceQuota do once attached to a Namespace?
options: It deletes Pods that have been running too long
It caps the total CPU, memory, or object count that namespace is allowed to consume, regardless of who submits the request
It grants a user permission to create Pods
It automatically scales Deployments inside that namespace
questions.explain: A ResourceQuota sets hard limits (e.g. requests.cpu, pods) on a namespace as a whole, protecting other namespaces sharing the same cluster.

questions.q: Two teams on the same cluster both create a Deployment named "worker" in their own separate Namespaces. What happens?
options: Kubernetes rejects the second Deployment outright
Both exist without conflict, since names only need to be unique within a Namespace, not across the whole cluster
The second Deployment silently overwrites the first
Both Deployments merge into one
questions.explain: Object names must be unique within a Namespace, not cluster-wide — this is exactly the collision problem Namespaces are designed to prevent.
